title: Economics Research Specialist in Economics and Economic Policy
description:
Description

The Department of
Economics at Dartmouth College invites applications for an
Economics Research Specialist, at the rank of Post Graduate
Research Associate. The ERS will support Professor
Heidi Williams with all stages of qualitative and quantitative
research related to economics and economic policy.

Responsibilities

Programming to construct and validate data
Undertaking descriptive and econometric analyses
Estimate economic models
Communication of qualitative and quantitative research in
writing
Assistance drafting and editing papers for publication

Economics Research Specialists (ERSs) will work with department
faculty supporting and conducting scholarly research and teaching
in anticipation of advancing their skills and experience to prepare
for the next stage of their careers. ERSs are expected to
contribute to all stages of research – including research design,
literature searches, conducting experiments, collecting and
analyzing data and writing reports and papers. ERSs may also have
opportunity to contribute in the classroom or in laboratory
sections of courses, helping undergraduate students with labs,
review sessions, paper editing and grading certain
assignments.

This position is full-time, expected to be non-remote, in-residence
for the Department of Economics at Dartmouth College in Hanover,
NH, with start date as early as June 2027. Remote positions may be
possible. Appointments are typically for a 1-year period with the
potential for renewal. Salary is $60,000 annually.

ERSs who are working in residence in Hanover, NH are eligible for

Graduate Special Student status and the ability to take certain
Dartmouth courses with the tuition paid by Dartmouth as a working
condition fringe benefit. The benefit covers a maximum of 1 course
per academic year the ERSs is employed and in residence at
Dartmouth.


Dartmouth is committed to academic excellence and encourages
the open exchange of ideas within a culture of mutual respect.
Dartmouth welcomes people with different backgrounds, life
experiences, and perspectives and believes that diversity in all
its forms enhances academic excellence. Applicants should address
in their application letter how their research, teaching, service,
and/or life experiences prepare them to serve Dartmouth’s
commitment to academic excellence in an environment that is
welcoming to all.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s in economics or a related field, completed by the
start of the appointment
A long-term interest in pursuing research related to economics
and economic policy
Experience and interest in constructing and analyzing data but
also in undertaking qualitative, institutional, and historical work
needed to interpret the data in context.
Previous programming experience (in languages such as R,
Matlab, Python, or Stata)
Demonstrated ability to work well collaboratively and
independently
Excellent attention to detail, problem solving skills, and
creativity
Strong writing and oral communication skills

This position is eligible for J-1 visa sponsorship for eligible
candidates. Employment is contingent on authorization to work in
the United States.

Application Instructions

1. Application letter that addresses:

Relevant research-related experience
Teaching or mentoring experience
Preparation to serve Dartmouth’s commitment to academic
excellence in an environment that is welcoming to all
Educational and career goals and how the position would advance
them.

2. CV/Resume

Name
Email and phone/text contact
Current position, or academic affiliation
Date of (expected) undergraduate degree
Academic concentration(s)
List all academic classes (and final grades) you have completed
that focus primarily on economics or economic policy
Include programming languages and/or software and levels of
proficiency.

3. Most recent academic transcript (unofficial transcript is
acceptable)

4. Three professional references with contact information

Review of applications will be on a rolling basis and will continue
until the position is filled. Recommendation letters will be
requested only for finalists. For questions about the position,
please contact Amy Rossi at amy.j.rossi@dartmouth.edu .

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

Dartmouth College is an equal opportunity employer under federal
law. We prohibit discrimination on the basis of race, color,
religion, sex, age, national origin, sexual orientation, gender
identity or expression, disability, veteran status, marital status,
or any other legally protected status. Applications are welcome
from all.

Dartmouth is committed to accessibility for its community. If you
are an applicant with a disability and would like to request a
reasonable accommodation to aid in the job application and/or
interview process, please email: ADA@Dartmouth.edu . In the subject
line, please state application accommodations and include the job

For additional employment opportunities at Dartmouth College,
please visit the Dartmouth Interfolio
Job Board , the 
Office of the Provost , and the Office of Human Resources
.

Offers of employment are contingent upon consent to a
pre-employment background check with results acceptable under
Dartmouth 
policy . Please visit the Dartmouth policy portal for faculty
